name: Persistent Fifth Aortic Arch

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Persistent Fifth Aortic Arch Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of a double lumen aortic arch demonstrated by imaging
Abnormal branching pattern of the aortic arch vessels
Presence of associated congenital cardiac defects such as ventricular septal defect or coarctation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a double lumen aortic arch with abnormal branching on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging findings; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Double lumen aortic arch detected by imaging
searchTerms: double lumen aortic arch seen on imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital systemic arterial obstruction due to persistent fifth arch
searchTerms: arterial obstruction from persistent fifth arch

common.symptomName: Respiratory distress secondary to vascular ring effect
searchTerms: trouble breathing from blood vessel compression
breathing difficulty caused by vascular ring

common.symptomName: Differential blood pressure between upper and lower extremities
searchTerms: different blood pressure in arms and legs
unequal arm and leg blood pressure
blood pressure varies between upper and lower limbs

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties due to esophageal compression
searchTerms: feeding problems due to throat compression
nerve problems from low blood flow
brain function loss due to poor circulation
neurological symptoms from reduced blood supply

imaging: Echocardiography showing double lumen aortic arch
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography demonstrating persistent fifth aortic arch
Angiography revealing abnormal aortic arch branching
other: Clinical examination revealing differential pulses and blood pressure
Cardiac catheterization findings consistent with arch anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Single aortic arch narrowing without double lumen
Typical site of narrowing distal to left subclavian artery
Complete vascular ring encircling trachea and esophagus
Usually involves double aortic arch or aberrant subclavian artery

redFlags: Marked differential cyanosis or blood pressure between limbs
references: Graham TP Jr, et al. Persistent fifth aortic arch: clinical and angiographic features. Am J Cardiol. 1989;64(8):790-794.
